in_hebrew.name: Isolde
in_hebrew.long_meaning: Isolde הוא שם נוצרי עם משמעות רוחנית עמוקה בתרבות הנצרות. The name Isolde is believed to have originated from the Welsh language and was derived from the names Isoldes or Iseultes. These names may have meant 'ice' or 'foreigner'. In Celtic mythology, Isolde was a legendary queen who was renowned for her great beauty and was the inspiration for many legends and stories. In Christian tradition, Isolde is remembered as a saint and is venerated for her faith and courage.

in_latin.name: Isolde
in_latin.meaning: Isolde, feminine given name of uncertain origin
in_latin.long_meaning: Name Isolde is derived from Old French name Yseut or Isaut, possibly from Latin Isolda, which is of uncertain origin. It may be derived from Old High German 'isal' meaning 'blessed' or 'divine', or from Old French 'yseut' meaning 'God is my oath'. In Christian tradition, the name Isolde has been associated with the legend of Tristan and Iseult, a tale of doomed love. The name has been used in various forms throughout history, including Isolde, Isolda, and Yseult. In modern times, the name Isolde has experienced a resurgence in popularity, particularly in Scandinavian countries.
